newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. agency says hunger growing in developed world.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency says hunger growing in developed world.

text.p: The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), in a report issued ahead of its food summit next month, said on Wednesday hunger was now also becoming a problem in industrialised countries.
The report cited a growing gap between the rich and the poor in developed countries and urged governments to do more to fight poverty.

"In the course of the 1980s and 1990s, as the distribution of income in the industrialised countries of North America and Europe has become more uneven and as social-welfare spending has been cut back in the face of rising unemployment, the need for food assistance among low-income groups has grown," it said.
The FAO report said hunger had become widespread in parts of the former Soviet Union, citing "malfunctioning markets, lack of safety nets and underemployment".

It also called attention to bad eating habits by many people living in industrialised countries which it said contributed to heart disease, obesity, hypertension, strokes, some types of diabetes, various forms of cancer and liver disease.

"Policy makers must recognise that poverty is a major cause of food insecurity and poor health...and that malnutrition leads to losses in productivity and the misallocation of scarce resources," the report said.
The agency said the report, "Food Security and Nutrition", was one of several technical background papers prepared in advance of the food summit to be held in Rome November 13-17.
It has said some 100 heads of state and government would be attending the final two days of the summit, convened to draw attention to the problem of world hunger.
